rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person's success before God depends on faith rooted deeply in the heart; outward profession alone carries no weight.
rows.anchor: To God, success of a person is entirely based on the faith that should deeply penetrate into the heart of a person.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is faith's foremost manifestation; faith that produces no prayer is barren, useful only as fuel.
rows.anchor: The foremost manifestation of faith is the prayer. Faith which does not yield the prayer is like a barren tree that can only be used to ignite fire.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humility of heart is prayer's real essence; prayer without it has no effect on a person's life.
rows.anchor: The real essence of the prayer is humility of the heart.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humble prayer restrains evil, vulgarity, and futile conduct; awareness of God's companionship in prayer protects a person from unbefitting acts.
rows.anchor: The prayer punctuated with humility stops a person from evil, vulgarity and useless activities. A person acquires God’s companionship in the prayer.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakāh is faith's second manifestation and prayer's second arm; together they are religion's two primary directives and the basis of all sharīʿah.
rows.anchor: These are the two premier directives of religion and all the sharī‘ah is based on these two.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi says Abū Bakr's campaign against those withholding zakāh followed from the principle that rejecting either primary directive undermines adherence to both.
rows.anchor: The attack launched by Abū Bakr (rta) against those who were desisting to pay zakāh was based on this philosophy of religion.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who submit heart and wealth to God do not let desire drive them beyond His limits or violate others' rights and honor.
rows.anchor: Those who submit their hearts and wealth to God never become so blind in following their desires that they break His limits

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faithful keep every trust and promise, whether owed to God or to other people.
rows.anchor: These people abide by all trusts and promises, whether they relate to God or to His creatures.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They carefully guard prayer, which acts like a wall protecting every part of their religion.
rows.anchor: They safeguard their prayer and their prayer is like a boundary wall that safeguards every aspect of their religion.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with these traits will dwell forever in God's Paradise; this is true success.
rows.anchor: Those who have the above-mentioned traits will in fact be the dwellers of God’s Paradise and will abide in it forever.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next sūrah, al-Nūr, supplements this one: faith illuminating the inner self brightens individual and collective life, while its absence darkens both.
rows.anchor: Details of all these points will be found in the next sūrah: Sūrah al-Nūr which is the supplement of this sūrah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding believers' glad tidings and the warnings implicit for faithless disbelievers are realities, though deniers of resurrection and the hereafter dismiss them as fantasy and mock them.
rows.anchor: The glad tidings given to the believers in the previous section are a definite reality. Similarly, the warnings they conceal for the disbelievers devoid of faith are also a definite reality.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi summarizes the earlier passage as a progression from inward faith through prayer, zakāh, restraint, fidelity, and guarded prayer to lasting success.
rows.anchor: on them depends the success of the believers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who reject resurrection and the hereafter treat the promised realities as imaginary and make fun of them.
rows.anchor: By presenting the objections of such people, attention is directed to the signs in their inside and outside world.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflection on the stages of human creation makes clear that the God who created people can readily recreate those who die and decay into dust.
rows.anchor: if a person only reflects on the phases of his creation it will become crystal clear that the God Who is capable of doing all this can have no difficulty in re-creating those who die and decay into dust.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The outer world shows that God continues to nourish humanity after creating it; this care makes it implausible that He would leave deeds unjudged, and points to reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: when He is undertaking all this in such an elaborate manner, how is it possible that He not hold people accountable for their deeds?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrection argument also appears in 22:5; this passage develops it further and elaborates aspects not treated there.
rows.anchor: This argument has also been stated in verse 5 of S ūrah al-Ḥajj.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi connects the creation stages here with 22:5: there they prove resurrection, and “so that We make evident for you” signals that the gradual sequence displays God's power and wisdom.
rows.anchor: There, the opening words were: ﺐٍ رَﻳۡ ﺘﻢۡ /.ۡ ﻛﻨۡ نۡ ﻣ	ﻦَ  ﻟۡﺒَﻌۡﺚ if you are in any doubt of being raised to life again

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stages of human development are familiar, and modern science has disclosed aspects the Qur'an only hinted at; further knowledge reveals more of these secrets.
rows.anchor: the more knowledge human beings gain, the more they know of these secrets.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A drop arising from clay is gradually nourished until it becomes people such as Socrates, Hippocrates, Aristotle, and Galen, prompting reflection on whether this elaborate process is accidental.
rows.anchor: ultimately, the likes of Socrates, Hippocrates, Aristotle and Galen are created. The question is: Is all this happening of its own accord?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence of creation, its care, and its evident power and wisdom cannot be meaningless products of uncontrolled matter; the One who forms a human from a drop can recreate that person.
rows.anchor: Is all this power, wisdom, providence and affection a meaningless thing which has no purpose and fate? Is the being Who fashions out a human being from a drop of fluid unable to create him again?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an directs people to inspect their own bodies and stages of development; reflection there supplies the answers without searching far afield.
rows.anchor: If they reflect on their own phases of creation, they will get all the answers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A new creation altogether” points to the astonishing transformation from a fluid drop into a living human, making denial of the Creator's power to resurrect unreasonable.
rows.anchor: The words “then We made it into a new creation altogether” point to the incredible nature of transformation a drop of fluid undergoes to become a living human being.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stages of creation should lead a reflective person to recognize God as blessed and beneficent: He turns an ordinary drop into a miraculous human endowed with extraordinary capacities.
rows.anchor: The God Who showed His signs, marvels and miracles in every person is blessed and beneficent

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity's remarkable stature is illustrated by the angels bowing to Adam and humans becoming God's vicegerents on earth.
rows.anchor: such are his abilities that angels bowed down to him and he became the vicegerent of God on earth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflection should establish not only God's existence but that the Creator is wise, beneficent, powerful, blessed, and peerless.
rows.anchor: a person does not merely acknowledge the existence of God, he is convinced that his creator is wise, beneficent, powerful, blessed and peerless.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The superlative afʿal, especially when annexed to a plural noun, can magnify an attribute rather than compare; “best of creators” means the Creator fashioned humans in the best mould with the best abilities.
rows.anchor: the superlative أﻓﻌﻞespecially when annexed to a plural noun, at times does not signify any comparison

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes alter the sense of “creator” because they miss this Arabic usage; Islahi rejects that change as unnecessary.
rows.anchor: Some exegetes have changed the meaning of the word “creator” because of not being aware of this style. Obviously, this is not the slightest needed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human creation refutes accounts based on uncontrolled matter, a prime mover, a first cause, or self-evolution; a blessed, outstanding Creator brought humanity into being.
rows.anchor: he has not been created by matter that is unbridled or by a prime mover or by a first cause nor has he evolved on its own.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The death and resurrection statements are the intended inference from the preceding creation stages: the God whose creative marvels people witness can raise them again.
rows.anchor: There is no reason to deny being raised to life again:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven skies are splendid and brilliant, and their description foreshadows the following profound discussion of rain.

rows.anchor: The word ﻛﻨ	َﺎ here expresses “majesty” as it does in ﺎﻤً ﻴْ ﺣَﻜ ﺎ ﻋَﻠﻴْﻤً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the account of human creation, the passage turns to God's providence: He did not become indifferent after creating people but sustains the world and its inhabitants through skies and rain.
rows.anchor: The previous verse mentions the creation of human beings, and the purpose is to point to the fact that recreating them is not at all a difficult proposition. Now in this verse God’s providence is referred to.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Measured rain gives life, while excess could devastate as in Noah's flood; God stores water in the earth as a reserve for living beings and could remove the entire supply.
rows.anchor: It is His mercy that He send it down in a specific measure otherwise it can wreak havoc if He allows it to.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exact rain sent from heaven for earth and its stored supply show that one intention governs both realms; separate controllers would not coordinate them this way, and this one Lord is merciful.
rows.anchor: both the heavens and the earth are being controlled by the same intention. If different intentions were controlling both, why would those in charge of the heavens send down water in such an exact quantity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi infers an omitted expression to the effect of “you reflect” after the mention of abundant fruit, treating the ellipsis as a familiar Arabic construction.
rows.anchor: The mention of ﺗَﺎۡshows that a word to the effect ﻬﻮْن ﺗَﺘَﻔَﻜ	َis suppressed after ﻓَﻮَ ﻛَﺜ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides more than basic subsistence: He gives people varied fruits for enjoyment as well as food; Islahi connects this to the ideal orchard Arabs knew from 18:32.
rows.anchor: A person could have lived on bread but God created it for him fruits of all sorts.
